LESSON: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: INSTRUCTION CHARTS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why should we give clear instructions?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. create instruction charts for information
2. appreciate the importance of clarity in written instructions

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts

Teach
• Focus skill: create instruction charts for information.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we give clear instructions?
2. what went well and why?
3. what did not go well and why?
4. what can be done differently next time?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
